'''Eli Ben-Sasson''' (Hebrew: אלי בן-ששון) is an Israeli computer scientist known for his work on [[zero-knowledge proofs]]. He is also the co-founder and CEO of [[StarkWare Industries]], a Founding Scientist of Zcash, and a former Professor of Computer Science at [[Technion – Israel Institute of Technology|Technion]].

== Career ==

Ben-Sasson studied [[theoretical computer science]] at [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]], earning his PhD in 2001 under the supervision of Prof. [[Avi Wigderson]].<ref name="radcliffe">{{Cite web|url=https://www.radcliffe.harvard.edu/people/eli-ben-sasson|title=Eli Ben-Sasson|website=Radcliffe Institute for Advanced Study at Harvard University}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=*Expansion in Proof Complexity* Thesis submitted for the degree Doctor of Philosophy by Eli Ben-Sasson |url=https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?repid=rep1&type=pdf&doi=7973565ac3851d2ae53d3f0aba094f3dbb08e365}}</ref> He then completed his Postdoctoral Studies at Harvard and MIT.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2024-11-27 |title=Geekonomy - פרק #974 – פרופ׳ אלי בן-ששון |url=https://geekonomy.net/2024/11/27/geekonomy974/ |access-date=2025-06-09 |website=Geekonomy |language=he-IL}}</ref><ref name="radcliffe" /> In 2005, Ben-Sasson joined the faculty of the Faculty of Computer Science at the Technion as Senior Lecturer (Assistant Professor). In 2009, he received the Henry Taub Award for Academic Excellence.<ref>{{Cite web |title=חדשות {{!}} הפקולטה למדעי המחשב טאוב, הטכניון |url=https://cs.technion.ac.il/he/news/view-new.php?nwid=363 |access-date=2025-06-09 |website=cs.technion.ac.il}}</ref> In 2010, Ben-Sasson was promoted to  Associate Professor at the Technion and in 2015 was promoted again to Full Professor, a position he held till he left Technion in 2020. He researched theoretical computer science and [[computational complexity theory]].<ref name=":0" /> 

In the early 2000s, Ben-Sasson published a series of articles on short, efficiently testable proofs, including [[PCP theorem|quasi-linear length PCP proofs]],<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Ben-Sasson In 2013, Ben-Sasson lectured about his research on Zero-knowledge proof at a Bitcoin conference and introduced the potential benefit of Zero-knowledge to Increase Bitcoin scalability.<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Q4nWoEKUtgU |title=Computational Integrity - applications to Bitcoin (ZCash pre-history) |date=2017-07-06 |last=Eli Ben-Sasson |access-date=2025-06-09 |via=YouTube}}</ref> He then met with early crypto pioneers, including [[Vitalik Buterin]] and Greg Maxwell, and raised awareness for the use of Zero-knowledge proof in crypto. Following that, he began working towards the practical realization of his research in the field of crypto and blockchain.<ref name=":0" />

In 2014, Ben-Sasson and other researchers collaborated on Zerocash, a design for a private [[cryptocurrency]] based on zero-knowledge proofs.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Ben Sasson |first1=Eli |last2=Chiesa |first2=Alessandro |last3=Garman |first3=Christina |last4=Green |first4=Matthew |last5=Miers |first5=Ian |last6=Tromer |first6=Eran |last7=Virza |first7=Madars |chapter=Zerocash: Decentralized Anonymous Payments from Bitcoin |date=2014 |title=2014 IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy |pages=459–474 |doi=10.1109/SP.2014.36|isbn=978-1-4799-4686-0 }}</ref> This research won the 2024 IEEE Test of Time Award.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-05-20 |title=White paper that birthed crypto ZK-proofs receives IEEE 'Test of Time' award |url=https://cointelegraph.com/news/whitepaper-birthed-crypto-zk-proofs-receives-ieee-test-of-time-award |access-date=2025-06-09 |website=Cointelegraph |language=en}}</ref> Ben-Sasson later became a founding scientist of [[Zcash]], which was based on the Zerocash design.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Zk-Starks? New Take on Zcash Tech Could Power Truly Private Blockchains |url=https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2017/09/30/zk-starks-new-take-on-zcash-tech-could-power-truly-private-blockchains |access-date=2025-06-09 |website=CoinDesk |language=en}}</ref>

In 2018, Ben-Sasson and other researchers invented STARKs and FRI protocols, which together created a type of [[zero-knowledge proof]] with several unique traits: (1) protection against quantum computers, (2) quasi-linear proof time, (3) polylogarithmic verification time, and (4) transparency, which means no dependence on secret keys.<ref>{{Citation |last1=Ben-Sasson |first1=Eli |title=Scalable, transparent, and post-quantum secure computational integrity |date=2018 |url=https://eprint.iacr.org/2018/046 |access-date=2025-06-09 |id=2018/046 |last2=Bentov |first2=Iddo |last3=Horesh |first3=Yinon |last4=Riabzev |first4=Michael}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=page |first=Sharon Wrobel You will receive email alerts from this author Manage alert preferences on your |url=https://www.timesofisrael.com/israeli-blockchain-firm-develops-fire-prevention-tech-to-thwart-ftx-style-fraud/ |access-date=2025-06-09 |website=[[The Times of Israel]] |date=8 February 2023 |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/ninabambysheva/2022/05/25/ethereum-scaling-company-starkware-quadruples-valuation-to-8-billion-amid-bear-market/ |access-date=2025-06-09 |website=Forbes |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-02-05 |title=Israel's Ethereum scaling tool Starknet Prover will be made open source |url=https://www.jpost.com/business-and-innovation/banking-and-finance/article-730653 |access-date=2025-06-09 |website=[[The Jerusalem Post]] |language=en |issn=0792-822X }}</ref> Later that year, Ben-Sasson co-founded [[StarkWare Industries]] alongside Uri Kolodny (who served as its first CEO), Michael Riabzev (his PhD student) and [[Alessandro Chiesa]]. StarkWare offers scaling solutions for blockchains using STARK techniques. Since February 2024 Ben-Sasson has been both CEO and president of the company.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-11-16 |title=עוד יוניקורן ישראלי נולד: סטארקוויר מגייסת 50 מיליון דולר לפי שווי של 2 מיליארד {{!}} כלכליסט |url=https://www.calcalist.co.il/calcalistech/article/sy2obf11dk |access-date=2025-06-09 |website=calcalist |language=he}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last1=שטרקמן |first1=רותם |last2=בוקסנבוים |first2=נעם |date=13 April 2018 |title=אלי בן ששון, פרופ' בטכניון, יצר מטבע דיגיטלי וחושב שהביטקוין גאוני |work=TheMarker Online |url=https://www.themarker.com/markerweek/2018-04-13/ty-article/0000017f-e15f-d7b2-a77f-e35f8cd50000}}</ref> 

In April 2019, Technion sued Ben-Sasson along with his PhD student and co-founder Michael Riabzev and others, alleging that StarkWare Industries was based on intellectual property developed at the university.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-04-23 |title=Technion sues own lecturer, claims intellectual property infringement |url=https://www.jpost.com/israel-news/technion-sues-own-lecturer-claims-intellectual-property-infringement-587672 |access-date=2025-06-09 |website=[[The Jerusalem Post]] |language=en |issn=0792-822X }}</ref> The institute demanded 50% of Ben-Sasson's stake in the company. Ben-Sasson maintained that the company used employees' knowledge and open source code, but no invention belonging to the Technion.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dobrovitsky |first=Lital |date=2019-04-22 |title=Technion Suing Senior Professor for 50% of His Company Stake |url=https://www.calcalistech.com/ctech/articles/0,7340,L-3760876,00.html |access-date=2025-06-09 |website=CTECH - www.calcalistech.com}}</ref> No patents or other IP claims were submitted by Techion since then, and in 2020 the two sides reached an agreement before the case reached the court.
